prompt: With the SVI administratively enabled, which two conditions must be true for interface Vlan20 to come up? (Choose two.)
options: IPv4 routing is enabled globally.
VLAN 20 exists and is active locally.
At least one other switch is connected by a trunk.
An eligible Layer 2 port in VLAN 20 is linked and STP forwarding.
A default route points toward an external router.
explanation: An SVI comes up (autostate) only when its VLAN exists and at least one Layer 2 port in that VLAN is up and STP forwarding. IP routing and routes are not required.

whyWrong.0: An SVI can come up for management with IP routing disabled.
whyWrong.2: One forwarding access port is enough, so no trunk is required.
whyWrong.4: A default route does not affect SVI line state.

prompt: Which two statements about ip default-gateway on a Cisco switch are correct? (Choose two.)
options: It supplies a host-style next hop while IP routing is disabled.
It installs an S* default route in the IPv4 routing table.
It supports the switch's own traffic toward other subnets.
It enables forwarding of user packets between SVIs.
It must be configured separately under every SVI.
explanation: ip default-gateway is a global, host-style next hop used when IP routing is off, for the switch's own traffic to other subnets. It does not forward user traffic and does not add a route to the table.

whyWrong.1: It is a host-style setting and does not create an S* route.
whyWrong.3: Forwarding between SVIs needs ip routing.
whyWrong.4: It is a global command, not a per-SVI command.

exhibit.title: Representative abbreviated interface status
exhibit.text:
Port       Status       Vlan     Duplex  Speed
Gi1/0/1    connected    10       a-full  a-100
Gi1/0/2    connected    20       a-full  a-100
Gi1/0/24   connected    routed   a-full  a-1000

prompt: What does the routed entry for Gi1/0/24 show?
options: It is a Layer 3 physical interface rather than a VLAN switchport.
It is a trunk that carries every VLAN with an SVI.
It is an access port in VLAN 24 with a gateway.
It is a VLAN 1 port forwarding only management traffic.
explanation: The port is a routed interface, configured with no switchport. It has its own IP address and is not a member of any VLAN.

whyWrong.1: A trunk is a Layer 2 port and would show as a trunk.
whyWrong.2: An access port would show its VLAN membership.
whyWrong.3: A routed port is not a Layer 2 port in VLAN 1.

prompt: A host pings its local management SVI and gets a reply. What does that test alone prove?
options: The switch routes all other connected VLANs.
The switch has a working default route.
Every trunk permits the host's VLAN.
The local host-to-SVI IP exchange works.
explanation: A reply from the SVI proves only that the host and the SVI can exchange IP packets in that VLAN. It does not test routing between VLANs, remote routes or trunks.

whyWrong.0: A switch answers at an SVI even when IP routing is disabled.
whyWrong.1: This local exchange needs no default route.
whyWrong.2: The path does not cross every trunk.

prompt: The router rejects an IP address on a new subinterface because no VLAN encapsulation is configured. The VLAN is 30. What do you do?
options: Enable the switch's VLAN 30 SVI and leave the router unchanged.
Assign the same IP address to the physical parent interface.
Enter encapsulation dot1Q 30, then re-enter the rejected address.
Rename the subinterface from .30 to .300 and repeat the address.
explanation: A subinterface needs encapsulation dot1Q before it accepts an IP address. A rejected address command is not saved, so enter it again after the encapsulation.

whyWrong.0: An SVI on the switch does not finish the router subinterface.
whyWrong.1: The design uses tagged VLAN 30 on a subinterface, not an address on the parent.
whyWrong.3: The subinterface number does not set the VLAN.

prompt: R1 routes an echo request from PC-A (192.168.10.11) to PC-B (192.168.20.12) with no NAT. What does the frame sent toward PC-B contain?
options: Source MAC R1's VLAN 20 interface; destination MAC PC-B; destination IP 192.168.20.12.
Source MAC PC-A; destination MAC PC-B; destination IP 192.168.20.12.
Source MAC R1's VLAN 20 interface; destination MAC PC-B; destination IP 192.168.20.1.
Source MAC PC-A; destination MAC R1's VLAN 10 interface; destination IP 192.168.20.12.
explanation: A router builds a new Ethernet frame on each link. The IP addresses stay the same and the MAC addresses change.

whyWrong.1: PC-A's MAC is not kept across the router.
whyWrong.2: The destination IP stays PC-B's address.
whyWrong.3: That is the frame PC-A sent to R1, not the one R1 sends out.

exhibit.title: Representative abbreviated DSW1 evidence
exhibit.text:
show vlan brief:
20   USERS20   active   Gi1/0/2

show interfaces status:
Gi1/0/2    notconnect    20    auto    auto

show ip interface brief:
Vlan20   192.168.20.1   YES manual   up   down

prompt: VLAN 20 is active, Vlan20 is not shut down, and Gi1/0/2 is its only member port. Why is the SVI down?
options: IPv4 forwarding is disabled globally.
VLAN 20 is missing from the VLAN database.
Vlan20 is administratively shut down.
Its only eligible Layer 2 member port is down.
explanation: An SVI needs at least one up and forwarding Layer 2 port in its VLAN. Gi1/0/2 is the only port in VLAN 20 and it is down.

whyWrong.0: IP routing has no effect on SVI autostate.
whyWrong.1: The exhibit shows VLAN 20 active.
whyWrong.2: The question states the SVI is not shut down.

prompt: A 2960 port toward a router-on-a-stick is set to dynamic auto. The router sends no DTP. What fixes the switch side?
options: Assign the router's gateway address to the switch's access port.
Configure a static trunk with the required VLANs and native treatment.
Enable dynamic auto on each router subinterface.
Set only the switchport trunk native VLAN, leaving the port in access mode.
explanation: The router never negotiates, so the switch port must be set to trunk statically. Allow the VLANs the subinterfaces use.

whyWrong.0: A switchport takes no gateway address.
whyWrong.2: Router subinterfaces do not run DTP.
whyWrong.3: A native VLAN does not turn an access port into a trunk.

exhibit.title: Representative host-mode routing display
exhibit.text:
Default gateway is not set

Host               Gateway           Last Use    Total Uses  Interface
ICMP redirect cache is empty

prompt: SW2 does not route IP. Its SVI is 192.168.99.10/24 and router 192.168.99.1 has the remote routes. SW2 has no next hop for return traffic. Which command supplies it?
options: ip default-gateway 192.168.99.1
interface vlan 99 followed by shutdown
switchport trunk native vlan 99
explanation: A non-routing switch uses ip default-gateway as the next hop for its own traffic to other subnets. ip route would work only with ip routing enabled.

whyWrong.1: A static default route is not used while IP routing is disabled.
whyWrong.2: Shutting the SVI removes management access.
whyWrong.3: The native VLAN does not supply a next hop.

prompt: Which sequence turns Gi1/0/24 on a multilayer switch into a Layer 3 interface at 10.0.12.2/30?
options: interface vlan 24 → ip address 10.0.12.2 255.255.255.252 → no shutdown
interface gi1/0/24 → switchport mode trunk → ip address 10.0.12.2 255.255.255.252
interface gi1/0/24 → no switchport → ip address 10.0.12.2 255.255.255.252 → no shutdown
interface gi1/0/24 → switchport access vlan 24 → ip default-gateway 10.0.12.2
explanation: no switchport turns the physical port into a routed port. You can then address it directly and enable it with no shutdown.

whyWrong.0: That configures an SVI, not the physical port.
whyWrong.1: A trunk stays Layer 2 when you add an address.
whyWrong.3: An access VLAN and ip default-gateway do not create a routed port.

exhibit.title: Representative excerpt — R1# show ip interface brief
exhibit.text:
GigabitEthernet0/0       unassigned      YES unset   up                    up
GigabitEthernet0/0.10    192.168.10.1    YES manual  up                    up
GigabitEthernet0/0.20    192.168.20.1    YES manual  administratively down down
GigabitEthernet0/1       unassigned      YES unset   administratively down down

prompt: VLAN 10 works. The trunk carries VLANs 10 and 20, and R1's encapsulation and addresses are correct. Which change fixes the VLAN 20 fault shown?
options: Add an IP address to the parent Gi0/0.
Enable unused Gi0/1 as a return interface.
Replace the VLAN 20 address with the VLAN 10 gateway.
Enter no shutdown under Gi0/0.20.
explanation: Gi0/0.20 is administratively down. Enter no shutdown on that subinterface.

whyWrong.0: The parent is intentionally unaddressed in router-on-a-stick.
whyWrong.1: The VLANs use Gi0/0, not Gi0/1.
whyWrong.2: The VLAN 20 address is already correct.

prompt: A switch must give several VLANs a gateway and route between them without a separate router trunk. Which design does that?
options: A router-on-a-stick with one shared trunk.
One access uplink with all hosts configured in different VLANs.
A Layer 2 trunk with every VLAN allowed.
SVIs on a multilayer switch with IPv4 routing enabled.
explanation: SVIs on a multilayer switch with ip routing enabled give each VLAN a gateway. The switch routes between them internally.

whyWrong.0: Router-on-a-stick depends on the separate router trunk.
whyWrong.1: An access uplink does not give several VLANs a gateway.
whyWrong.2: A trunk extends VLANs but does not route.

prompt: Vlan30 has an address and no shutdown but is down. VLAN 30 is missing from the VLAN list, though the access port is still assigned to it. What do you fix first?
options: Apply no shutdown to Vlan30 again.
Create and activate VLAN 30 in the VLAN database.
Enable IP routing without restoring VLAN 30.
Change the host's gateway address.
explanation: An SVI stays down while its VLAN is missing from the VLAN database. Create VLAN 30, then check that a port in it is up and forwarding.

whyWrong.2: IP routing does not replace a missing VLAN.
whyWrong.3: A host setting cannot create a VLAN on the switch.

prompt: SW1 sends native VLAN 99 traffic untagged to R1. Which subinterface command tells the router that untagged traffic is VLAN 99?
options: encapsulation dot1Q 99
switchport trunk native vlan 99
encapsulation dot1Q 99 native
switchport access vlan 99
explanation: encapsulation dot1Q 99 native makes the subinterface handle untagged frames as VLAN 99. Without native, it matches only tagged VLAN 99.

whyWrong.0: Without native, the subinterface matches only tagged VLAN 99.
whyWrong.1: That is a switch command, not a router subinterface command.
whyWrong.3: That is a switch access-port command.

prompt: PC-A (192.168.10.11/24, gateway 192.168.10.1) pings 192.168.20.12 with an empty ARP cache. What is the destination MAC of its first ARP request?
options: The broadcast address ffff.ffff.ffff.
PC-B's MAC, obtained from the remote destination IP.
The local switch port's burned-in MAC address.
The gateway's MAC, already inferred from its IP address.
explanation: A host sends an off-subnet packet to its gateway, so it ARPs for the gateway's MAC. An ARP request is a broadcast to ffff.ffff.ffff.

whyWrong.1: PC-B is on another subnet and the host never ARPs for it.
whyWrong.2: The switch port is not the next hop.
whyWrong.3: With an empty cache, the gateway's MAC is not yet known.

exhibit.title: Representative DSW1 evidence
exhibit.text:
Vlan10   192.168.10.1   YES manual   up   up
Vlan20   192.168.20.1   YES manual   up   up

show ip route:
Default gateway is not set

prompt: DSW1 has working SVIs for VLANs 10 and 20, but ip routing is not configured. What is missing for the two subnets to reach each other?
options: A static default route toward the other SVI.
The global ip routing command.
An address on each Layer 2 access port.
Set ip default-gateway to the VLAN 10 host address.
explanation: A multilayer switch forwards IPv4 between its SVIs only after the global ip routing command. Without it the switch acts as a host.

whyWrong.0: The subnets are directly connected, so no default route is needed.
whyWrong.2: The gateway addresses belong on the SVIs, not on access ports.
whyWrong.3: ip default-gateway helps only the switch's own traffic.

prompt: DSW1 routes connected VLANs 10 and 20 and has no default route. What follows?
options: The VLAN traffic is being switched without a Layer 3 decision.
The hosts must use the routed uplink address as their gateway.
Connected routes are sufficient for those destinations; other destinations need matching routes.
The hosts must have a /16 mask to compensate for the missing default.
explanation: Each VLAN's subnet has a connected route, so DSW1 needs no default route for those subnets. Other destinations need their own routes.

whyWrong.0: Traffic between subnets is routed, not just switched.
whyWrong.1: Each host uses a gateway in its own subnet.
whyWrong.3: Widening the mask would make hosts ARP for remote hosts directly.

exhibit.title: Supplied link evidence after a cable move
exhibit.text:
Gi0/0       unassigned      down  down
Gi0/0.10    192.168.10.1    down  down
Gi0/0.20    192.168.20.1    down  down
Gi0/0 configuration: no shutdown; unchanged valid subinterface settings

prompt: Every subinterface on Gi0/0 is down. What do you check first?
options: The physical Gi0/0 connection and its switch peer.
The IP mask on every host at the same time.
The native VLAN number on each access port.
A default route between the connected VLANs.
explanation: All subinterfaces depend on the parent interface. If the parent is down, they are all down, so check its cable and switch port first.

whyWrong.1: Host masks do not affect the router's interface state.
whyWrong.2: Native VLAN settings do not cause a down physical link.
whyWrong.3: A route cannot bring up a down interface.

exhibit.title: Supplied complete relevant SVI state
exhibit.text:
VLAN 20 exists and is active; Vlan20 is enabled
All local VLAN 20 access ports: down
Gi1/0/24: operational Layer 2 trunk, link up
VLAN 20: allowed, active and forwarding on Gi1/0/24
No autostate overrides are configured

prompt: Under normal autostate, can Vlan20 stay up with this state?
options: No; only a local access port counts toward SVI state.
Yes; an SVI stays operational whenever it has an IP address.
No; a VLAN needs both an access port and a trunk before its SVI works.
Yes; the forwarding trunk can provide an eligible VLAN 20 member.
explanation: An SVI needs at least one up and forwarding Layer 2 port in its VLAN. A trunk port that carries VLAN 20 counts.

whyWrong.0: Access and trunk ports both count.
whyWrong.1: An IP address alone does not bring an SVI up.
whyWrong.2: One eligible port is enough, so no mix is required.

exhibit.title: Supplied host and switch checks
exhibit.text:
PC-B: 192.168.20.12/24; default gateway blank
PC-B pings local peer 192.168.20.13 and SVI 192.168.20.1
DSW1: ip routing; correct connected VLAN 10 and 20 routes
Other correctly configured hosts communicate between those VLANs

prompt: PC-B cannot reach VLAN 10 hosts. Which fix follows from the checks?
options: Replace PC-B's /24 mask with /16.
Assign the gateway address directly to PC-B.
Set PC-B's default gateway to 192.168.20.1.
Move PC-B into VLAN 10 without changing its address.
explanation: PC-B reaches its own subnet but has no default gateway for other subnets. Set it to the VLAN 20 SVI at 192.168.20.1.

whyWrong.0: A /16 mask would make PC-B ARP directly for the remote VLAN.
whyWrong.1: The SVI already owns that address, so PC-B would conflict with it.
whyWrong.3: Moving PC-B breaks the addressing design.

prompt: A Layer 2 access switch cannot route. A router has one Ethernet interface for three VLANs. Which design fits?
options: Three gateway SVIs on the Layer 2-only switch.
A switch trunk to three addressed router subinterfaces.
One routed switch port per VLAN.
A single untagged router interface with no VLAN separation.
explanation: Router-on-a-stick runs all VLANs over one trunk to the router. Each subinterface gives one VLAN its gateway.

whyWrong.0: A Layer 2 switch cannot route between its SVIs.
whyWrong.2: The switch cannot route, and the router has only one link.
whyWrong.3: One untagged interface cannot separate three VLANs.

exhibit.title: Supplied new-VLAN acceptance evidence
exhibit.text:
Plan: VLAN 30, subnet 192.168.30.0/24, gateway 192.168.30.1
PC-C: 192.168.30.11/24, gateway 192.168.30.254 (unused)
PC-C access port: VLAN 30; VLAN active
SW1 trunk: VLANs 10,20,30,99 allowed/active/forwarding
R1 Gi0/0.30: encapsulation dot1Q 300; IP 192.168.30.1/24; up/up
Existing VLAN 10 and 20 tests pass

prompt: Two mistakes stop the new VLAN 30 host from working while VLANs 10 and 20 work. Which two changes fix them? (Choose two.)
options: Set the router's .30 encapsulation to VLAN 30.
Replace the switch uplink's allowed list with VLAN 30 only.
Set PC-C's gateway to 192.168.30.1.
Change the router parent to an access switchport.
Rename .30 to .300 while leaving its encapsulation unchanged.
explanation: The router's .30 subinterface has the wrong VLAN tag, and PC-C points to the wrong gateway. Fix the encapsulation and set the gateway to 192.168.30.1.

whyWrong.1: The allowed list already includes VLAN 30, and replacing it would break VLANs 10 and 20.
whyWrong.3: The router's parent interface must stay a trunk-facing routed interface for the subinterfaces.
whyWrong.4: The subinterface number does not set the VLAN tag.

exhibit.title: Supplied complete relevant evidence
exhibit.text:
DSW1: ip routing; Vlan10 192.168.10.1/24 up/up
DSW1 routed Gi1/0/24 10.0.12.2/30 up/up; R2 peer 10.0.12.1/30
PC-A 192.168.10.11/24 gateway 192.168.10.1; local gateway ping passes
DSW1 ping sourced from 10.0.12.2 to 10.0.12.1 passes
R2 complete routes: only 10.0.12.0/30 connected and its local address; no default
No traffic filters in this lab

prompt: DSW1 pings R2 from its link address, but a VLAN 10 host's ping to R2 fails. What do you check next?
options: Change the working routed port into a trunk.
Check R2's return route to the host subnet.
Replace the host gateway with R2's off-subnet address.
Create VLAN 12 because the link uses 10.0.12.0/30.
explanation: DSW1's ping uses a source in R2's connected /30, which works. The host's source is in 192.168.10.0/24, and R2 has no return route to it.

whyWrong.2: The host should use its local SVI as its gateway.
whyWrong.3: A routed link's network does not need a matching VLAN.

prompt: What is an SVI?
options: A physical routed port with no switchport
A logical Layer 3 interface for a VLAN
A trunk subinterface on a router
A static route to a VLAN
explanation: An SVI is a switch virtual interface. It gives a VLAN a logical Layer 3 interface.

whyWrong.0: That describes a routed port made with no switchport.
whyWrong.3: An SVI is an interface, not a route.

prompt: Does an ordinary trunk between two switches route traffic between VLANs?
options: Yes, because tagging adds a gateway to the link.
Yes, but only for traffic in VLAN 1.
No, it only carries VLANs; a Layer 3 device routes.
No, because trunks drop frames from other VLANs.
explanation: A trunk preserves VLANs and does not route between them. A router or multilayer switch must route.

whyWrong.0: Tagging labels frames and adds no gateway.
whyWrong.1: Trunks route no VLAN, including VLAN 1.
whyWrong.3: A trunk carries frames from many VLANs.

prompt: A host sends a packet to an off-subnet destination. Which destination MAC is in the Ethernet frame?
options: The destination host's MAC
The broadcast address
The default gateway's MAC
The switch's MAC
explanation: A host sends an off-subnet packet to a gateway in its own subnet. The frame uses the gateway's MAC.

whyWrong.0: The remote host's MAC is not reachable from this subnet.
whyWrong.1: A broadcast is used for ARP, not for data.
whyWrong.3: The switch forwards the frame and is not its destination.

prompt: Which router feature carries several VLANs over one physical interface in router-on-a-stick?
options: Subinterfaces
Port channels
SVIs
Loopback interfaces
explanation: Each router subinterface uses encapsulation dot1Q to map one VLAN on the shared trunk link.

whyWrong.1: A port channel bundles links and does not split VLANs.
whyWrong.2: SVIs are logical interfaces on a multilayer switch.
whyWrong.3: A loopback is not tied to a physical link.
